Process:

1. Pick smallest character from s -> append, remove it.
2. Then, keep picking smallest character from s which is greater than last appended character and append until can't.

So after initial pick, we keep going ascending: each step pick next larger char than last appended. Essentially we pick an increasing sequence of distinct chars? Not distinct necessarily; but if smallest appears multiple times, we can choose any occurrence. But step 2 says smallest character which is greater than the last appended character, so strictly greater. So ascending without equal. So we pick each distinct char in ascending order once each time if count >0? Actually if duplicates exist, we only pick one of each character in ascending until can't. But duplicates of same char: they wouldn't be picked because strictly greater. So effectively we pick each unique char at most once as we ascend.

Then step 4: pick largest character from s and append it (now use remaining characters). Step 5: pick largest character from s which is smaller than last appended. So moving descending. So we pick the largest, then descending distinct chars until can't.

This process repeated until all characters removed. Effectively we produce sequence: ascending sequence of distinct available chars, then descending sequence of distinct available chars, repeating.
